summary: 1951 steel fire tower on Mount Toby, Sunderland, Mass.; open to the public with a locked cabin and climbable outside stairs; staffed seasonally per 2016 visit reports.

facts.design: Current 68-foot steel tower with a wooden cab per NHLR

access.note: Wikipedia calls the tower open to the public; Trailspotting says the cabin is locked but the outside metal stairs can be climbed.

facts.agency: Mass. Bureau of Forest Fire Control

visit.trail_note: Trailspotting describes the Blue Trail, which follows the power lines to the tower, from the Cranberry Pond trailhead.

events.note: Original 58-foot structure destroyed by the 1938 hurricane (NHLR)
68-foot steel tower replaced it; that tower later blew down (NHLR)
Current 68-foot steel tower with wooden cab went into service (NHLR)
Cabin last replaced in 2002, per the Fire Lookout Association as relayed by Trailspotting
Visit report dated April 8, 2016 describes the tower as staffed seasonally

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR describes a 58-foot structure on Amherst Agricultural College land; Trailspotting describes an open wooden platform. Both are reported as descriptions of the first structure; the story does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1951 build year checks out. The 1938 to 1951 sequence comes from one source (NHLR). Two Facebook posts from the Fire Lookout Association appeared in search results (one dated a 1923 tower, one a 1950 build) but could not be read, so they are not used and the sequence may need a second check. Access: Wikipedia says open to the public; Trailspotting (November 2024) says the cabin is locked and the outside stairs can be climbed. The Wikidata entry (Q107454486) only gives a label and is not used.
